title: Nearly two in three tweens and teens have used a chatbot
friendlyTitle: Nearly two in three children and teens have used a chatbot
summary: NPR reported on 30 October that two surveys put chatbot use well above half of American tweens and teens. Common Sense Media found that nearly half of 9-to-12-year-olds have used a chatbot or companion, and that by 13 nearly three-quarters have. A JED Foundation survey of 5,500 students aged 9 to 17 found that 90 percent have used one, and that nearly two-thirds use chatbots both for schoolwork and when they are stressed, lonely, or anxious.
friendlySummary: NPR reported on 30 October that two surveys found chatbot use is common among American children and teens. Common Sense Media found that nearly half of 9-to-12-year-olds have used a chatbot, and that by age 13 nearly three-quarters have. Most popular chatbots set 13 as the minimum age. A separate survey of 5,500 students aged 9 to 17 found that 90 percent have used one. Nearly two-thirds use chatbots both for schoolwork and when they feel stressed, lonely, or anxious.
whyItMatters: JED says students who turn to a chatbot while in distress are more likely to report poor mental health and a history of suicidal thoughts. It also says the survey does not show whether the chatbot contributes to that distress or whether students already in distress are the ones who turn to it. A University of North Carolina researcher, not involved in the surveys, told NPR that separate not-yet-published work found companionship use linked with growing lonelier over time. The practical step is to ask what the chatbot is being used for, not only whether it is used.
